events.title: The Council of Nicaea proclaims the Creed
events.shortBlurb: The first ecumenical council, gathered against Arianism, confessed the Son to be “consubstantial” with the Father…
body: In 325 the emperor Constantine, newly master of the whole Roman world, summoned the bishops of the Church to Nicaea in Bithynia to end the controversy that troubled the East. Arius, a priest of Alexandria, taught that the Son was a creature, made out of nothing and not co-eternal with the Father.

About three hundred bishops — later tradition fixed their number at 318 — gathered that June, nearly all from the Greek East; Pope Sylvester was represented by two priests, and Hosius of Corduba presided. Against Arius the council confessed the Son to be 'begotten, not made, consubstantial (homoousios) with the Father,' and appended anathemas to its creed.

The creed of Nicaea, expanded at Constantinople in 381, is still professed at Mass. The council's twenty canons ordered the Church's discipline, and its settlement that Easter be kept on one and the same Sunday everywhere remains the basis of the Christian calendar.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), General Church history
